title: Ledger Epistemology and Regime-Closure Governance: An Operational Framework for Validation in Coupled Multi-Scale Systems
description: Presents a five-component operational framework to prevent narrative reabsorption in validation of coupled multi-scale systems: explicit regime tagging, frozen-parameter governance, sealed pre-registered predictions with cryptographic hashes, a public falsification ledger, and external arbitration. The framework is field-tested within the Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) programme (163 DOIs, 135 registered tests, 11 falsifications; validation ledger v4.6) and shown to be portable across domains (medicine, economics, metrology).

key_results.main_finding: A five-component governance machine is introduced and operationally demonstrated to block internal narrative reabsorption in complex, coupled multi-scale validation, with feasibility evidenced by the EFC programme’s public ledger (v4.6), 163 DOIs, 135 registered tests, and 11 documented falsifications.

kill_criteria: KC1: Documented instance of internal narrative reabsorption occurring in a test that had all five components in place (regime tagging, frozen-parameter governance, sealed pre-registration with cryptographic hash, public falsification ledger, and external arbitration) without a corresponding recorded model/governance update.
KC2: Absence, removal, or alteration of failed sealed predictions from the public falsification ledger (i.e., failure to preserve failed predictions with documented failure modes).

KC3: Violation of frozen-parameter governance evidenced by retroactive parameter changes across datasets/regimes after a sealed prediction is deposited, without recording the change as a model extension.
KC4: Inability to verify pre-registration via cryptographic deposit hashes linking prediction statements to their deposits (e.g., missing or unverifiable hashes).

KC5: External arbitration outcomes being decided within the originating apparatus (no independent arbiter as pre-specified), or arbitral decisions subsequently reinterpreted within the originating narrative to avoid model/governance revision.
